messages:
jamal: heads-up: customer acme-inc reporting p95/p99 spikes since ~02:10 UTC. our dashboards show GPU mem pressure on pool-7 and a couple OOMs. tail latency 2-3x for generate route. escalating.

morgan: saw the same, p99 jumped from ~380ms to ~1.2s on generate.v1. Which tenants exactly?

jamal: acme-inc + 3 smaller tenants pinned to pool-7. KV size growth ~+40% last hour. logs show repeated kv reallocation + slab compaction churn. snippet: ```
[2026-03-16T02:12:08Z] INFO kv: evict_attempts=0 kv_bytes=1.9GB slab_used=92% OOM_count=2
[2026-03-16T02:12:09Z] WARN allocator: failed_alloc 128MB try_compact=true
```

ben: can you grab `nvidia-smi` + allocator stats? `/proc/<pid>/smaps` and `rd/allocator/stats` would help. also which model size is in use for the affected routes?

jamal: grabbing now. model is xlarge-quant (mixed). attaching quick allocator dump: ```
alloc_slab_total=2048MB
alloc_frag=18%
kv_entries=324k
kv_bytes=1.92GB
slab_compact_ops=47/5m
```

tara: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) enable fallback routing for the generate route to smaller model variant (xlarge-quant-lite) 2) reduce `batch_max_tokens` to 32 for affected tenants 3) toggle `slab_compaction=aggressive` on nodes in pool-7 to release fragments faster 4) temporarily bump the eviction aggressiveness.

alex: long-term: our `kv_high_water` at 0.85 is too permissive for this workload. lower to 0.7 and set `kv_eviction_threshold=0.6` so eviction triggers earlier. also consider per-tenant kcache caps and journaling KV growth for debugging.

jamal: applying `slab_compaction=aggressive` on node-12 now, rolling patch to allocator (reduce max_chunk -> 64MB) scheduled to start in ~2m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout allocator-tune/v2 to pool-7 — canary 1/3 (node-12). monitoring p95/p99.

morgan: after compaction + canary, p99 dropped to ~650ms, p95 back to ~300ms. OOMs stopped for node-12, but KV still creeping on other nodes.

ben: I'll run synthetic repro that mimics long-contex prompts and KV-heavy soft-state to exercise the growth path. running: ```./stress_kv --rps 120 --ctx-length 2048 --profile > kv-stress.log``` will post findings.

tara: if KV growth continues we should: A) force route to quantized 8-bit variant to shrink KV footprint, B) add a soft caps + eviction watermark per-tenant, C) schedule allocator-defrag job weekly.

jamal: pinging support & CS to notify acme-inc. @morgan please add this to the incident doc and set postmortem owner. include customer-facing mitigation steps and ETA.

morgan: on it. incident doc updated. action items: owner=ben, follow-ups=[allocator tuning, kv_eviction retune, routing rule update].

ben: quick note from stress run: when we push many long-context requests back-to-back we see incremental kv_bytes growth and occasional failed_allocs before compaction finishes. root cause feels like slow slab coalescing + large max_chunk. will keep updating.

jamal: thanks team. told customer we applied compaction + routing fallback; monitoring. will update once p99 stable for 30m. :thumbsup:

morgan: added final note to thread: if we don't see sustained improvement by +1h, escalate to infra oncall for emergency allocator rollback.

jamal: closing loop for now — p99 trending down. will reopen if any regression.
